stemMd: A café found that customers using reusable cups bought more drinks per month than other customers. The owner concluded that reusable cups cause people to drink more coffee. Which alternative most weakens that conclusion?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Frequent customers are more likely to buy a reusable cup.

options.label: B
options.textMd: The café opens six days a week.

options.label: C
options.textMd: The cups are available in several colours.

options.label: D
options.textMd: The café serves tea as well as coffee.

explanationMd: The observation is correlational. If frequent customers choose reusable cups because they already buy many drinks, the causal direction can run from frequent visits to cup ownership. This alternative undermines the claim that the cup itself increases consumption.

distractorRationale.c: Colour variety does not explain the observed association.
distractorRationale.d: This alone does not address the direction of causation.
distractorRationale.e: Serving temperature is irrelevant to the causal inference as stated.
distractorRationale.b: Opening days do not explain why cup owners differ from others.
